title: Astro Portal API v1 observation sessions and supplements
description: An observation session is the append-only record of a night: a resource plus a journal of events (session-event-ingest.schema.json) and, when field data arrives after a plan was frozen, proposed supplements. "Session" here always means an observation session; a browser authentication session is called a web session throughout this contract. Event bodies are never part of the session resource; a reader pages them separately. See api/v1.md, section "Observation sessions and debriefing".

executionId.description: Additive: the identity of one execution of a night that carries several plans, a ULID the client generates once; every observation session launched together for the plans of that execution carries the same one, one session per plan as always. Null for an execution of a single plan.

piloting.description: Additive: how the plan of this observation session is piloted — `mount` (the application points a mount), `smart_telescope` (the plan runs in a smart telescope), `assisted` (manual pointing assisted by a phone's plate solving, possibly with a satellite phone), `free` (the person drives the equipment; the plan is a reference). Null when not told. Written at the creation and changed afterwards by `PATCH /v1/sessions/{id}` (the mode of a night changed in « Nuit en cours »).

closedBy.description: Additive: how the night was closed, told by the phone when it finishes the session — `automatic` (the night closed by itself at its end) or `manual` (the person's own « Terminer »). Absent or null: unknown (a session that never said, an earlier one, a debriefing's or an import's). Written with the finish and never moved by a replay of it; a reopen clears it.

createRequest.description: POST /v1/sessions. `planId` is the server plan UUID, never a browser client id. `clientSessionId` is the caller's own idempotency key for a direct (plan-less) session; a plan-linked session is idempotent on `planId` alone. `executionId` and `piloting` (additive) are written when the session is created; a replay returning an existing session never changes them. Additive: `origin` says where the session is created from. Only `execution` (the default), `astro-sync` and `capture` (the night of a capture the person adds, built by the client as `POST /v1/sessions`, `POST /v1/sessions/{id}/finish`, `PATCH /v1/sessions/{id}/night`) are accepted; `debrief` and `import` are set by the service's own creation paths and answer `400 invalid_request`; an existing session returned by a replay never changes its origin.

pilotingRequest.description: PATCH /v1/sessions/{id}: the mode of a night changed in « Nuit en cours ». `piloting` is one of the four values and is required; the answer is the session `resource` with the new value. The same value again changes nothing.

resource.description: `updatedAt` is the server-side high-water mark of the observation session: the latest of its own creation, its finish, and the `receivedAt` of its newest event or supplement. It is the cursor `GET /v1/sessions?since=` compares against. Additive: `outcome`, `origin`, `projectId`, `eveningDate`, `reworkRevision` and `reworkedAt` are written by the service on every answer; they are optional in the schema only so that a reader of an earlier answer still validates (such a reader assumes `outcome: null`, `origin: "execution"`, `projectId: null`, `reworkRevision: 0`, `reworkedAt: null`).

projectId.description: The multi-night plan (`project.schema.json`, internally a « project ») the session belongs to: the link carried by the session's plan item of the session's target first (`planItem.projectId`), else the link the session carries itself (a night met in the field, a session without a plan attached afterwards), else `null`. A session with several targets of several multi-night plans reports the plan of its first target in the order of its plan.

reworkRevision.description: The revision of the session's rework (`session-rework.schema.json`): 0 at creation, +1 on each `PUT /v1/sessions/{id}/rework`. It is the value of `If-Match` the next rework must send.

reworkedAt.description: When the last rework was saved; `null` while there was none. `updatedAt` moves to this instant with each rework, so a reader that follows `GET /v1/sessions?since=` sees a reworked session again.

readOnly.description: Additive: `true` for a catalogue night of a private server (an opaque identifier `catalogue:<date>:<target>`, origin `import`), which nothing writes to. Written only when `true`; absent reads `false`.

deletedAt.description: Additive: when the session was deleted. Written only for a deleted session (the answer of its deletion and of `GET /v1/sessions?deleted=include|only`); a live session carries neither this nor `purgeAt`.

purgeAt.description: Additive: when the maintenance erases a deleted session: `deletedAt` plus 30 days.

createResponse.description: POST /v1/sessions. `created` is false when an existing observation session was returned instead of a new one (200 rather than 201) — the "no duplicate session" guarantee.

list.description: GET /v1/sessions. `nextSince` is the `updatedAt` of the last returned session and is meant to be sent back verbatim; the `since` bound is inclusive, so a client may see a session twice and never misses one.

deleteResponse.description: `DELETE /v1/sessions/{id}`: the session, deleted softly (it carries `deletedAt` and `purgeAt`), how long the space keeps it (`graceDays`, 30) and the whole days left (`daysRemaining`). Idempotent. `409 session_not_finished` for a night in progress.

restoreResponse.description: `POST /v1/sessions/{id}/restore`: the session, live again. A session that was not deleted is returned as it is. `409 session_plan_taken` (with the `sessionId` that holds the plan) when the plan has another session since.

erasure.description: `POST /v1/sessions/{id}/erase`: the definitive, immediate erasure of a session that was deleted. `erased` counts what went with it: its `captures` (their files and their lines of « Intégrations » included), `events`, `supplements`, `analyses`, `steps`, `packageImports`, `deviceJournalLines` (the journals Astro Sync sent) and `integrations` (the declared or measured lines of its multi-night plans). `409 session_not_deleted` for a session that is not deleted.

finishRequest.description: POST /v1/sessions/{id}/finish. An absent `finishedAt` means the server instant. A replay never moves an already recorded `finishedAt`. Additive: `closedBy` says how the night was closed (`automatic`: it closed by itself at its end; `manual`: the person's own « Terminer »); absent means unknown, and a replay never moves it either. Any other value answers `400 invalid_request`.

reopenRequest.description: POST /v1/sessions/{id}/reopen (« Reprendre la nuit »): a finished session is open again, `finishedAt` cleared, while its plan is not debriefed. `reopenedAt` is the instant of the gesture on the device (absent: the server instant). Idempotent: a session that is not finished is returned unchanged. A replay older than the recorded `finishedAt` (a later stop already won) is returned unchanged too, and a `finish` whose `finishedAt` is older than the last `reopenedAt` is ignored: the latest gesture wins whatever the order of arrival. A session whose plan is frozen (debriefed) is refused: 409 `session_debriefed`.

supplement.description: Late field data that reached a plan already frozen. `payload` is the submitted plan payload, stored verbatim and never rewritten; `eventIds` names the events an acceptance appended.

supplementDecisionRequest.description: POST /v1/sessions/{id}/supplements/{sid}. `dismiss` never deletes the payload; a dismissed supplement can still be accepted later, an accepted one can no longer be dismissed because its events are already appended.

detail.description: GET /v1/sessions/{id} (additive). `events` is the first page only, in the same shape GET /v1/sessions/{id}/events returns. It also carries the structured night (`night`, `steps`, `qualitySummary`, `guidingSummary`, `guidingSeries`), never gated by a capability. Additive: `events` are the **effective** events (the append-only journal read through the correction layer of the rework: added events with `timing: "reconstructed"`, moved events, without the events a rework removed; `session-event-ingest.schema.json`, `storedEnvelope.rework`), and `targets` the cards of the session. `GET /v1/sessions/{id}/events` reads through the same layer. This is also the answer of `PUT /v1/sessions/{id}/rework`. Answers also for the opaque identifier of a catalogue night of a private server (`readOnly: true`).

debrief.description: Additive: the debriefing stored with this session's plan — its outcome, instant and per-target adjustments, `acquiredMinutes` included. Null for a direct session and for a plan not debriefed yet.

debriefSummary.description: Additive: the summary of the night, computed at request time from the plan's items, the whole journal, the stored debriefing and, when shown, the guiding losses — never stored.

guidingLosses.description: Additive: the guiding losses of the night, present when the service holds an analysis of this session — whoever reads it (reading an analysis is never gated; `analysis.logs` gates its creation only). Null otherwise, with `guidingLossesReason` saying why; `debriefSummary` then has no guiding line.

guidingLossesReason.description: Why `guidingLosses` is null: `no_analysis` (no analysis of this session). Null when the losses are shown.

plan.description: A READ-THROUGH projection of the plan this observation session was generated from, resolved at request time and stored nowhere else. It is how the "equipment pre-filled" requirement is honoured without a second source of truth: `equipment` is the frozen plan payload's own `equipment` object, echoed verbatim, and `revision` names the exact revision it was read from, so an interface can show the night's equipment beside the journal without the session ever carrying a copy that could drift. `nightStartAt` is the origin the plan's time slots were counted from, which is what lets a reader place a `planned` event back on the night's timeline. Null for a direct session.

night.description: Additive: the night's own fields, each with its source.

steps.description: Additive: the night's acquisition steps, in their order.

qualitySummary.description: Additive: null without an analysis or without a quality row.

guidingSummary.description: Additive: null without an analysis or without guiding.

guidingSeries.description: Additive: the night's guiding by slices of about 2 minutes — the report's own slices, or computed from its samples; empty without guiding.

guidingTrace.description: Additive (w61): the night's guiding at one point per 10 s with the corrections and the markers — the report v3's `guidingTrace` as sent, or rebuilt from a report v2's raw samples (then `raPulseMs`/`decPulseMs` are null: the v2 does not say which way the corrections went, and `scaleArcsecPerPx` is null); null without guide samples (an import, a night without PHD2).

posesSummary.description: Additive (w61): the night's frames kept and left out by the stacking; null without an analysis or without a quality row.

zone.description: Additive (w61): the zone of the night's place and its offset at the night's start, for writing every instant in the place's hours (« heure du lieu »); both null when the place has none (the hours are then written in UTC, and said so).

targets.description: Additive: the session's targets in the order of the night, as the Journal draws them (`journal.schema.json`, `target`): planned, added and removed ones, with the figures taken from the debriefing, then the events, then Astro Sync's analysis. Empty for a session with neither plan nor event.

readOnly.description: Additive: `true` when the session is a catalogue night of a private server that `GET /v1/journal` lists (`readOnly: true`): no plan, no event, no supplement, its targets and nothing else; every write to it answers `409 session_read_only`. `false` for every other session.

nightSource.description: Where a field of the night comes from: `night` when the night holds it (the person set it, or it is the night's own like its start), `plan` when it is read through the night's plan because the person never set it.

nightPlace.description: The night's place: a name and, optionally, coordinates (never published). Never a time zone (the place rule): a reader shows instants in the viewer's own time. Read through the plan, `name` is the plan place's name or locality and may be null.

nightEquipment.description: The night's equipment: identifiers of the space's equipment (manage-equipment.schema.json) or of the platform's default equipment.

night.description: The structured night, in GET /v1/sessions/{id} and the PATCH answer: each field with its value and its `source`. `title` null: the screen titles « Nuit du mer. 7 oct. »; `notes` is the night's note (the field notes stay events of the journal).

nightPatchRequest.description: PATCH /v1/sessions/{id}/night, by the owner's web session (CSRF) or a device token of the space: the fields named are written, the others untouched; `null` gives a field back to the plan. `place` has no time zone (a `timeZone` is refused, 400). `finishedAt` only once the night is finished (409 `night_not_finished`). Unknown equipment or target: 422 `equipment_not_found`, `target_not_found`.

step.description: One acquisition step of the night (`acquisition_steps`): target (catalogue or personal; null when unknown, `targetHint` keeping what the frames said), filter (the person's free text, never normalized; null reads « Sans filtre »), frames, exposure, gain, and the integration computed (frames × exposure, never entered). `origin`: `analysis` (proposed by Astro Sync's analysis), `import` (the old nights' import) or `manual`. `edited`: corrected by hand (« modifié »); a new analysis replaces the `analysis`/`import` steps never edited and keeps the others. `stepKey` is the report's key of a proposed step.

stepCreateRequest.description: POST /v1/sessions/{id}/steps: a step added by hand (origin `manual`). 201 with the `step`.

stepPatchRequest.description: PATCH /v1/sessions/{id}/steps/{stepId}: a correction by hand; the step is marked `edited`. DELETE on the same path removes it (204). Unknown step: 404 `step_not_found`.

qualityFigures.description: Medians of the measured frames: FWHM in pixels, and in arcseconds when the report knows the scale (`pixelScaleArcsec`; « 2,6 px · 8,1″ »), eccentricity, sky background and its noise in ADU, stars detected; `measuredFrames`, the frames holding at least one measure. A figure no frame gave is null.

qualitySummary.description: The night's quality, computed at read time from its analysis, never stored: for the night and by step (`stepId`, the night's step proposed under that key, null when it no longer exists).

guidingSummary.description: The night's guiding, computed at read time from its analysis: root-mean-square in right ascension, declination and total over the night (arcseconds; from the raw samples, or the slices weighted by their samples), the guided duration, the samples, dithers, expired settles, focus runs launched and succeeded, meridian flips. Dithers are counted once: an ASIAIR dither within 30 s of a PHD2 dither is the same one (a report v2 holds it twice). Additive (w61): `starLost`, the star losses (those within 30 s one), and `guideScaleArcsecPerPx`, the guide camera's scale when the report v3 gives it; the RMS is the report v3's own `guidingTrace.rms` when it has one.

posesSummary.description: The night's frames (the quality rows of its analysis): `total`, `kept`, `rejected` (left out by the stacking: `byReason` counts them by `rejectReason` — `unregistered`, `dawn`, `sky`, `clouds`, `trailed`, `wide`, `manual`), their exposure in seconds (`totalSeconds`, `keptSeconds`), and the same by filter (`byFilter`, `filter` null for « Sans filtre »). `rejectedKnown` is false for a report v2, which never said which frames the stacking left out: all count as kept.

nightZone.description: The zone of a night's place (IANA, `Europe/Paris`) and its offset east of UTC in minutes at the night's start (`120`), for the readers that cannot read a zone's rules; both null when the place has none.

outcome.description: Additive: how the night turned out, `null` while it does not say. `executed` (the plan was carried out), `partial` (in part), `abandoned` (the plan was not carried out: the night is kept as a finished session with its reason). Taken from the debriefing of the session's plan; `null` for a session not debriefed yet and for a session without a plan (an observation made freely, an import): those have no promise to compare with. Never written by a client on the session itself: the debriefing (`debrief.schema.json`) is the only way to set it.

origin.description: Additive: where the session was created. `execution` (the phone's or the web's « Nuit en cours »; also what a reader assumes for a session that does not say), `debrief` (created by a debriefing of a plan carried out or not carried out without the application), `import` (an import: the package of a night, the old portal's nights, a night rebuilt from captures), `astro-sync` (created by Astro Sync's « Nuits »), `capture` (created when a capture is added with no session to join, for the night and the place of the photo; finished at once, editable like any session, never read-only, and not an import). Set once, by the creation path, and never changed.

eveningDate.description: The night's date (`YYYY-MM-DD`), **the definition of the integrations** (`integration.schema.json`, `eveningDate`): the plan's date when the session has a plan, else the evening of its start at the place's longitude, local noon to local noon (12:00 UTC minus longitude / 15 h), UTC noon when no longitude is known. Never a time zone. `capture.nightDate` (`capture.schema.json`) keeps its own definition (the night of the capture's plan, else of its session) and is not changed.
